content.title: World Baseball Classic final preview: Venezuela vs. USA
content.text: The 2026 World Baseball Classic final is upon us.Team USA punched its ticket Sunday night with a win over the Dominican Republic and will face Venezuela, which defeated Italy on Monday night. The U.S. and Venezuela are matching up in the WBC championship now on FOX.Before the U.S. faces Venezuela, here's everything you need to know about the final.World Baseball Classic Championship Game: Venezuela at United States When and where: 8 p.m. ET tonight at loanDepot park in Miami.How you can watch: The World Baseball Classic championship game will air live on FOX.How you can listen: There is a free English-language audio stream available for every Classic game.Who's going to pitch?: Mets righty Nolan McLean will get the starting nod against Venezuela. The 24-year-old allowed three earned runs in three innings vs. Italy in pool play, but he had a 2.06 ERA in 48 innings down the stretch for the Mets last season.For Venezuela, left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez was announced as the starter. In his lone appearance in this tournament against the Dominican Republic in Venezuela’s final game in pool play, Rodriguez allowed three runs in 2 2/3 innings, allowing a pair of home runs to Juan Soto and Ketel Marte.1. Bobby Witt Jr., SS2. Bryce Harper, 1B3. Aaron Judge, RF4. Kyle Schwarber, DH5. Alex Bregman, 3B6. Roman Anthony, LF7. Will Smith, C8. Brice Turang, 2B9. Byron Buxton, CF1. Ronald Acuña Jr., RF2. Maikel Garcia, 3B3. Luis Arraez, 1B4. Eugenio Suárez, DH5. Gleyber Torres, 2B6. Ezequiel Tovar, SS7. Wilyer Abreu, LF8. Salvador Perez, C9. Jackson Chourio, CFHow they got here: Team USA defeated the Dominican Republic, 2-1, on Sunday to advance to its third straight Classic final. It was a tense game in which every run came via a home run. Gunnar Henderson hit a game-tying homer to lead off the third inning, then Roman Anthony clubbed a go-ahead solo shot two batters later. The lone run for the D.R. came via a Junior Caminero homer in the second. Righty Paul Skenes tossed 4 2/3 innings for the U.S., scattering six hits and allowing just the one run, before five relievers held the D.R. to just two hits the rest of the game and stranded the tying run at third base in the ninth.Venezuela beat Italy 4-2 in a semifinals thriller on Monday, using a three-run seventh inning to take the lead and secure a second straight comeback win. Ronald Acuña Jr. tied it in the seventh inning with an RBI infield single before Maikel Garcia gave the Venezuelans the lead for good with a go-ahead RBI single. After starter Keider Montero allowed two runs in 1 1/3 innings, Venezuela's bullpen tossed 7 2/3 scoreless innings. In its previous game in the quarterfinals against Japan, Venezuela also used a dramatic comeback to overtake the reigning WBC champions.Because the teams entered the finals with the same 5-1 record, home-field advantage was determined by a coin flip, which went in favor of the United States.What’s at stake: The winner will be crowned the 2026 World Baseball Classic champion. Team USA won its only WBC championship in 2017, when it defeated Puerto Rico, 8-0, in the title game. Meanwhile, this will be Venezuela's first WBC title game appearance.Matchup history: These two squads have met five times in Classic play, with the U.S. holding a 3-2 advantage. Their first meeting came in 2009 pool play, when the U.S. won a 15-6 blowout that included homers from Kevin Youkilis, Adam Dunn and Ryan Braun. Their last meeting came in the 2023 quarterfinal, which the U.S. won 9-7 thanks to a go-ahead grand slam from Trea Turner.Jason Foster is a reporter for MLB.com.Skenes back to Cy Young form in win after tough Opening Day start7:33 PM UTCCINCINNATI -- Pirates ace Paul Skenes rebounded from the shortest outing of his career to post five strong innings Wednesday and earn his first win of the season, 8-3, against Cincinnati at Great American Ball Park.After allowing five runs on four hits, walking two and hitting a batter while retiring just two batters last Thursday, Skenes (1-1) allowed just one run on three hits, striking out five and walking two. He tossed 77 pitches (51 strikes) and lowered his season ERA from 67.50 to 9.53. Skenes left with a 4-1 lead thanks to an Oneil Cruz three-run homer off Cincinnati starter Andrew Abbott (0-1) in the first. Pirates Home Opener is Friday vs. the Orioles -- Get your tickets now! Mason Montgomery relieved Skenes to start the sixth, and allowed a pinch-hit two-run homer to Eugenio Suárez as the Reds cut the Pirates’ lead to one run. But Isaac Mattson, Justin Lawrence and Gregory Soto finished off the final 3 1/3 innings for Pittsburgh’s first series victory of the season.The Pirates have Thursday off before their home opener Friday afternoon against Baltimore.Bryan Reynolds blasted a two-run homer deep to the seats in right in a four-run ninth for his 140th as a Pirate, moving him into sole possession of ninth place all-time in Pirates history.Skenes didn’t give up a hit until Elly De La Cruz swatted a 90.1 mph changeup to right field for a single to open the bottom of the fourth. After Sal Stewart’s grounder moved De La Cruz to second, Nathaniel Lowe doubled him home, snapping Skenes’ scoreless streak against Cincinnati at 31 innings, dating to his first career start against the Reds on June 17, 2024.Coming into Wednesday’s game, the opponent figured to be the perfect elixir for the flame-throwing Pittsburgh ace after his shortest career outing six days earlier against the Mets in Queens.In five previous starts against the Reds, Skenes was 4-0 with a 0.31 ERA, covering 29 innings. He struck out 40 and walked just two batters. Skenes had not allowed a run against Cincinnati since the first inning of his first start against the Reds.Like his Opening Day start last Thursday, Skenes had an early lead to work with, this time thanks to Cruz belting his third homer of the series and season, and his second in as many at-bats.With two outs, Reynolds singled and Marcell Ozuna walked. Cruz then hopped all over a hanging curve from Abbott and unloaded it a Statcast-projected 407 feet to right for a 3-0 Pirates lead in the first.Skenes needed a batter to find his rhythm, walking leadoff man TJ Friedl on five pitches. But unlike his outing against the Mets, he quickly found a groove, striking out Matt McLain and De La Cruz before retiring the red-hot Stewart on a force out at second.
